nm_sandia_mountains.blurb: The Sandia Mountains are Albuquerque's big backyard range, and the climbing on their west face is mostly traditional, with a good number of alpine-style lines and only a little sport, ice and bouldering. The rock is ancient granite capped by a thin limestone band, and it turns slippery when wet. Routes run from short canyon lines to long ridge and wall climbs of up to ten or more pitches. Most grades fall between 5.7 and 5.12, with 5.9 to 5.11 the most common. Approaches are long and route finding and runouts are common, so solitude is typical. The high crest climbs best from about May to October, while the warm west-facing walls can be dry on winter days. The big canyons include La Cueva, Chimney, Nova and Echo.

ny_h_southern_mountains.blurb: The Southern Mountains cover the southern Adirondacks of New York, with crags along the Route 10 corridor near Caroga Lake and Arietta plus cliffs around Lake Pleasant and Piseco Lake. More than half of the climbing is bouldering, led by Nine Corner Lake, the region's biggest boulder field, with Pinnacle Pullout nearby. Most problems fall between V0 and V5, with a thin tail of harder ones. The roped climbing is mostly trad, with a good amount of sport at places like Lost Hunters, and State Brook is one of the larger trad crags. Roped grades run from 5.5 to 5.13, with 5.10 the most common. The crags are scattered among lakes and woods rather than packed into one cluster.

va_shenandoah_national_park.blurb: Shenandoah National Park runs along the Blue Ridge in Virginia, and most of its climbing is on Old Rag, a peak near Sperryville with a rocky summit instead of the usual forested top. The rock there is granite, with splitter cracks, dihedrals and slabs. Routes are short, roughly 50 to 100 feet, from beginner to expert difficulty. Trad is the largest share of the climbing, with boulders close behind, and only a little sport and top-roping. Boulder problems mostly sit between V0 and V4. Roped grades run from easy fifth class to 5.12, with 5.9 to 5.11 the most common. Smaller pockets are spread through the park's Central, South and North Districts and around White Oak Canyon.

nm_socorro_area.blurb: The Socorro Area is climbing country in New Mexico, and nearly all of it sits in one box canyon southwest of the town, which the local tourism page calls the premier spot. The rock is volcanic. Sport climbing leads, with a large bouldering scene and smaller amounts of trad and top-roping. Roped grades run from easy fifth class to the low 5.13s, most often in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, while boulder problems lean toward V0 to V5. It is best known as a winter destination, with mild desert days in the 50s and 60s while many other areas are buried in snow. Summer can be hot and buggy.

bc_cheakamus_canyon.blurb: Cheakamus Canyon lies along Highway 99, roughly halfway between Squamish and Whistler. It is almost entirely a sport climbing area, with a few boulders and a little trad. The granite is tighter and more compact than at Squamish itself, so expect hard, smooth face climbing and few splitter cracks. The climbing is steep and often pumpy and juggy, and there is enough overhanging, sheltered rock to climb on rainy days at some crags. Grades are strong: 5.10, 5.11 and 5.12 are about equally common, with a good tail of 5.13s and a few 5.14s. Chek is the main area, with Rogues Gallery just north, and The Gorge and The Hideout are smaller sectors.

nm_box_climbing_areas_the.blurb: The Box is a canyon of cliffs and boulders near Socorro, New Mexico, built from rhyolite of uneven quality, though much of it is solid. The surface is smooth in places and sharp or pocketed in others. Sport routes dominate, with plenty of moderate bolted lines, and the bouldering is a big draw. Trad and top-rope climbs are a small share. Roped grades run up into the low 5.13s, clustered at 5.10 to 5.11, and boulder problems lean toward V0 to V5. The Southern Box areas are the busiest, the Northern Box areas have streambed boulders and walls, and Spook Canyon is a separate smaller pocket. Winter is the prime time on mild days; summer can be hot and buggy, though shade exists.
